intent: Keep the ±0.08 m, 0.04 m spacing, 0.016 m footprint array that removed line loss, and make the robot turn more readily by narrowing the wheel track, shortening the body and lightening the chassis. Target: max_error below 0.06 m and progress up on the s-bend and slalom, while keeping the oval finish rate at or above 55%.
learning: Hypotheses: (1) With line loss solved by the ±0.08 m array, the remaining off-track failure is turn-response lag, so a narrower track and lighter, shorter body should cut max_error below 0.06 m on the s-bend and slalom. (2) The 0.016 m footprint is adequate, since rms_error is 0.021 with no line loss, so sensor_size stays fixed. (3) A narrower track adds turn authority and may raise oval steering_oscillation; if it passes 0.25 while max_error improves, the next step is sensor y 0.05 to 0.03. Please report per-track values, especially max_error and progress on the s-bend and slalom, so the drift can be checked separately from oval oscillation.
rationale: Iteration 3 (±0.08 m span, 0.04 m spacing, 0.016 m footprint) fixed the line loss it was designed to fix. The s-bend and slalom now have 0 line-loss events per run, down from 0.6 and 0.95, and rms_error fell to 0.021 to 0.022. The score still fell from 272 to 210 because the oval finish rate dropped from 55% to 45%. Every track still ends off_track, with max_error 0.062 to 0.062 at the 0.06 m floor, and progress on the s-bend and slalom is only 0.18 and 0.09. The robot now stays on the tape but drifts past the 0.06 m limit without losing sight of it, so the limit is now the robot's steering response, not sensing coverage. Oval steering_oscillation fell to 0.16, so the sensor-lead change (y 0.05 to 0.03) is not triggered. Moving the sensors would not address drift that is not oscillation, so I leave y unchanged. body_width cannot help, since the off-track limit is already at its floor. Geometry can change turning response: turn rate is the wheel-speed difference divided by wheel_track, so a narrower track gives more turn per PWM count. Yaw inertia is mass*(L²+W²)/12, so a shorter, lighter body turns more readily. I therefore keep the validated sensor array (±0.08 at 0.04 m, 0.016 m footprint) and reduce wheel_track from 0.12 to 0.10 m, body_length from 0.16 to 0.12 m, and mass from 0.8 to 0.7 kg. Expected result: max_error below 0.06 m on the s-bend and slalom, progress rising on those tracks, and the oval finish rate at or above the 55% of iteration 2. The risk is more steering gain, which may raise oval steering_oscillation above 0.25; if it does, the next step is sensor y 0.05 to 0.03.
